headline.caveat: press-cited cumulative 2019–2023 investment; Microsoft filings disclose $13.0B of funding commitments. Converted Oct 2025 into ~27% of OpenAI Group PBC valued ~$135B

realized_to_date.caveat: funded portion per Microsoft 10-K disclosure; remainder of the commitment includes Azure compute credits

nature_md: Microsoft's 2019/2021/2023 investments (~$13.8B press-cited; $13.0B committed / $11.9B funded per 10-K disclosures, a substantial part delivered as Azure compute credits rather than cash) converted in OpenAI's Oct 28, 2025 recapitalization into ~27% of OpenAI Group PBC on an as-converted diluted basis, valued ~$135B — down from 32.5% of the old for-profit before dilution from subsequent rounds. Microsoft retains IP access through 2032, including post-AGI models (AGI declarations subject to an independent expert panel). Because Microsoft equity-methods the stake, its filings are the only public window into OpenAI's P&L: Q1 FY26 disclosures implied an OpenAI quarterly loss of ~$11.5B (The Register), and FY26's -$4.7B 'other, net' was mostly OpenAI equity-method losses. Microsoft's FY26 10-K also disclosed $24.1B of revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI and $6.0B of receivables.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: Equity-method investment: Microsoft recognizes its share of OpenAI's losses in other income (expense), net — FY26 'other, net' of -$4.7B was predominantly OpenAI losses, capping reported EPS. The funded-vs-committed gap and the credits component mean the cash cost is lower than the headline.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Equity financing plus, historically, Azure credits (in-kind compute rather than cash). No revenue to OpenAI; the credits directly funded compute consumption that Microsoft books as Azure revenue — the original template for equity-for-compute circularity.

both_sides_md: **Bear:** Microsoft's own statements quantify the problem — it booked $24.1B of FY26 revenue from a counterparty whose losses (~$11.5B/quarter implied) it simultaneously absorbs through equity-method accounting; revenue and losses from the same handshake. **Bull:** a ~$13B outlay is now a ~$135B stake (Oct 2025 mark) plus $24.1B/yr of high-margin related revenue — arguably the single best corporate investment of the decade regardless of OpenAI's near-term losses.

observations.method_md: Microsoft disclosed a $3.1B equity-method hit from OpenAI in its Sept-2025 quarter; grossing up by Microsoft's ~27% as-converted share implies OpenAI lost ~$11.5B in the quarter. Assumes Microsoft recognized its full proportional share with no basis-difference adjustments.

observations.notes: Related-party disclosure in Microsoft's FY26 10-K; accounts receivable from OpenAI were $6.0B at June 30, 2026.
